newsitem.title: CHINA: China's EximBank to extend more preferential loans.
newsitem.headline: China's EximBank to extend more preferential loans.

text.p: China's Export-Import Bank (EximBank) will extend more preferential loans to help promote cooperation between Chinese and overseas enterprises, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Practice in the past two years had shown that subsidised preferential government loans not only benefited economic development in the recipient country, but also Chinese enterprises to tap into overseas markets and compete internationally, it quoted a bank official as saying.
Therefore, the EximBank would expand its business in re-lending subsidised preferential government loans, which are long-term or medium-term loans provided to developing countries, he said.
The government decided to promote the use of preferential loans as assistance to developing countries in 1995 and designated the EximBank to handle the relending, Xinhua said.

EximBank has agreed to relend preferential loans to 32 projects in 24 countries in Africa, Asia, Oceania, and Latin America. It has already signed loan agreements for 15 projects, with the relending amount totalling 1.2 billion yuan, it said.
